name: Mourinhismo (merged with resultadismo): result-first, opponent-specific pragmatism
scopeNote: MERGE (user decision): resultadismo (Capello, Scolari, Deschamps) is folded into mourinhismo, which stays separate from low-block-counter-attack. Shared core: result first, plan and system chosen per opponent and squad, compact defence plus counters, no fixed style. Mourinho is the core exemplar (Porto 2002-01-23 to 2004-06-02; Chelsea first spell 2004-06-02 to 2007-09-20; dates from manager/jose-mourinho.json). Resultadismo exemplars: Capello Milan 1991/92-1995/96 (month-level start 1991-06; exact dates not checked), Scolari Brazil at the 2002 World Cup (June 2002; spell dates not checked), Deschamps France (evidence 2014 to the 2022 final, 2022-12-18; appointment date not checked). profilePeriod is therefore the union 1991-06 to 2022-12-18 with gaps between exemplars; each fact is dated by its own eventDate inside a counted window. Partial dates used where the day was not found. Sources use 'tactical periodisation' (Mourinho training), 'tactical flexibility', 'adapt according to opponents', 'pragmatic', 'futebol de resultados' (Brazil), 'resultadismo' (Spanish; Solari says the word is not in the dictionary). Popular labels 'parking the bus' and 'catenaccio' are not used by the sources: Mourinho's Porto/Chelsea also pressed-and-countered with a 4-3-3 or diamond, Capello kept Sacchi's zonal 4-4-2 base but dropped the full-pitch press, and Scolari's three centre-backs were meant (per Edmilson) to raise attacking volume. Distinct from low-block-counter-attack (Inter 2010 / Leicester 2016, a block-shaped idea): here the defining element is the result-first, opponent-specific plan and man-management, not a fixed block. Resultadismo is also a pejorative for short-termism in Argentina/Spain (Perfil, Solari), a different sense not profiled. Evidence is almost entirely tier C; no tier A study of any exemplar found.
openQuestions: Proposed ids not in catalog: team 'porto-2003-04' and 'chelsea-2004-05' (no team files exist for Porto or Chelsea); manager id 'jose-mourinho' exists.
Second Chelsea spell (2013-06-03 to 2015-12-17, Premier League 2014-15) left out of the window to keep the exemplar to Porto and Chelsea 2004-07; decide whether to include it.
Pressing intensity at Porto: thechels.info claims 'pressao alta' (page unreadable); the mined sources describe a block with counters, so the pressing label is unconfirmed.

Formation disagreement: Bleacher Report says Porto mostly 4-3-3; Sports Gazette says a diamond in the 2004 final; M&G says 4-3-3 was favourite. Consistent with per-opponent change, but base shape is contested.
Quotes 'I think am the Special One' and 'After God, me' come only via a 2020 retrospective; primary press-conference transcripts not found.
Psychological management is mostly tier C narrative (siege mentality, mind games); no tier A coach-written source found.

Is 'resultadismo' a tactical ideology at all? Solari (El Pais) questions the word itself and notes it can mean defensive, rigid, elastic or not interested in possession; we use it as 'result first, adapt to opponent/squad'.

Scolari 2002 pragmatism label: Edmilson says the 3-5-2 was to add attacking volume, Lucio says defensive security, a Brazilian academic piece called it overly defensive; sources disagree on the motive.
Capello Milan marking (zonal vs mixed) and Scolari/Deschamps marking not verified by any page read; Deschamps' 2012-2026 spell dates and Scolari's exact World Cup spell dates not checked.
Deschamps himself says (Orange/Figaro 2025, search summary only) that without play you cannot win over time, which contradicts the 'only victory' label; not verified.
Exemplar ids fabio-capello and didier-deschamps have no manager file in the catalog yet; luiz-felipe-scolari exists.

Naming: does the merged ideology still fit the name 'mourinhismo'? Resultadismo is a stance (result first) that Capello, Scolari and Deschamps share with Mourinho, but Solari questions the word, and 'result-first pragmatism' or 'pragmatismo/resultadismo' may be more neutral. Decision left to the user.

Is the merge sound? Mourinho's distinguishing traits (scouting dossiers, siege mentality, press mind games) are not documented for Capello, Scolari or Deschamps; the common ground is only 'result first, adapt to opponent/squad'. Mourinho and Deschamps overlap in the 2004 Champions League final (Porto 3-0 Monaco, Deschamps as Monaco coach).

Set-piece marking of Mourinho's Porto/Chelsea 2004-07 still not found. FourFourTwo (2010-11, Real Madrid) says he 'prefers zonal rather than man-to-man marking', outside the period so unverified; Record's 2006/07 Chelsea scouting dossier on Porto shows the staff recorded opponents' marking (Porto: zone on corners, man-to-man on free kicks) but not Chelsea's own.

Capello Milan marking: Goal (ES/ID) summaries describe a zonal 4-4-2 moving away from man-marking, but the mined paragraphs did not carry it, so zonal remains unverified; Coverciano 1984 paper on zonal marking is search-summary only.

Deschamps set-piece defending: no verified source (reports of conceding twice from corners vs Denmark and training drills are search summary only); France's attacking set pieces are verified for 2018.
